column1: # What each COPY --from in the Dockerfile's final stage puts into the released
# image. Keyed by source path rather than by build stage: one stage can supply
# several components under different terms, and a stage name is a refactorable
# label with no stability contract.
# The generator fails when the final stage copies from a path with no row here,
# so a new component cannot reach the image without an attribution decision.
# disposition:
#   project          built from this repository; its dependencies are already
#                    covered by the Dependency Index, so it is not listed again
#   first-party      NVIDIA's own software, which is not third party to NVIDIA
#                    and so is out of scope for this document
#   third-party      redistributed third-party software; license text reproduced
# The guard covers every copied path regardless of disposition, so first-party
# and project components are still accounted for here even though neither is
# listed in the document.
# version: literal, or ${ARG} to read that ARG's default from the Dockerfile.
# Use "-" where the build does not pin one and none has been established.
# provenance_digest: for a version recorded by hand rather than read from the
# build, the digest of the image that version was observed in. The generator
# fails when that digest is no longer in the Dockerfile, so bumping the builder
# forces someone to re-check the version instead of shipping a stale one.
# Use "-" when the version comes from the Dockerfile itself.
# license_file is relative to tools/licenses/ and must exist for third-party
# rows. source_url is the corresponding source, which a copyleft license
# obliges us to offer.
# source_path
